requirement: Implement StreamXmlRecordExtractor using lxml.etree.iterparse with events=('end',) and target tag filtering to parse arbitrarily large XML streams with constant memory overhead. Ensure both element.clear() and parent detachment (del parent[0]) are executed for each yielded record to prevent dead element accumulation, and validate target_tag inputs.
skeleton: StreamXmlRecordExtractor class with __init__ and iter_records using lxml.etree.iterparse.

rationale.teaches: Streaming XML with iterparse on end events filtered by tag, clearing each element and detaching it from its parent so memory stays constant, with a validated target tag.
rationale.why: iterparse without clear keeps every parsed element in the tree, so memory grows linearly but the yielded records are correct. The fixture measures memory over a large stream.

candidates.why_wrong: elem.clear() is omitted, so each record's subtree stays in memory after being yielded.
The parent check is inverted, so records are never detached and the tree grows with every record.
start events are used, so each record is yielded before its children are parsed and its text is empty.
The tag filter is dropped, so every end event is yielded, including child elements.
An empty target tag is accepted, so iterparse receives an empty filter and yields nothing.
